newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Che-hwa said he would announce who to join his new government by the end of the month. He set six criteria he would use to pick his team.
-- Meeting U.S. senators, Chinese President Jiang Zemin said Sino-U.S. relations had improved, but asked the United States to handle the Taiwan issue carefully.
-- MING PAO -- Although China's Vice-premier Zhu Rongji has tried to keep a low profile, five of his speeches on economic development have become popular among mainland officials and intellectuals.

-- At Wednesday's Legislative Council hearing over the forced retirement of former director of immigration Laurence Leung, the head of the civil service W.K. Lam is expected to stress that the government had made its decision based on a report from the Independent Commission Against Crime, and that it had no political implications.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chinese government-owned China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Ltd was operating in the territory for 10 years but had never registered with the Law Society according to Hong Kong law. When pushed, it argued it was not a foreign practice. While all legal practices in the territory are unlimited companies, China Legal Service insisted on remaining limited.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The People's Bank of China announced it had decided to shut down the China Agri-business Development Trust and Investment Corp for its involvement in serious illegal business activities resulting in huge losses.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A top Hong Kong insurance brokerage executive said China's plans to regulate its re-insurance market were likely to keep insurance costs artificially high.
-- Chinese corporate bonds, having lost their glitter since 1993, looked set to receive a mixed reception this year, despite plans for a bumper issue.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- U.S. company Bay Networks and the China Internet Corp, controlled by Beijing's Xinhua news agency, formed a partnership, China Wide Web, to design and implement a nationwide intranet in China.
